messages.content: Now that both flights are ticketed, finish the Philadelphia hotel. I need Sunday, October 18 through Thursday, October 22, one room for me. Please compare the full four-night cost, not just the nightly rates.

I have two refundable options. The Logan is the closer one: $996.00 for four nights, $140.00 in mandatory destination fees, and $176.08 in taxes, for a complete total of $1,312.08. Sofitel Philadelphia at Rittenhouse Square is $916.00 for four nights with no mandatory property fee and $141.98 in taxes, totaling $1,057.98. Sofitel is $254.10 less overall.
What are the ratings, and which source are those from? I want this to be a nice stay, so keep it at 4.0 or better.

Both meet that floor on the same metric. The Logan is rated 4.4 out of 5 on Google, and Sofitel Philadelphia is rated 4.5 out of 5 on Google. Those are guest-facing Google ratings, not hotel star classifications.
Good. Verify the Monday morning trip from each hotel to the Philadelphia Museum of Art. I need to be there by 8:15.

From The Logan, the museum is about 0.6 mile away. The practical route is west on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway and then toward the main entrance; allow roughly 12 to 15 minutes on foot, so leaving at 7:55 a.m. gives a small buffer. From Sofitel, walk about three minutes to the Route 38 stop near 19th and Walnut, take the westbound bus directly along the Parkway, and get off by the museum. The scheduled ride plus walking is about 18 to 23 minutes; I would leave by 7:40 a.m. to account for normal weekday variation.
So the Sofitel route does not require a transfer?
Correct. It is one SEPTA Route 38 bus with no transfer, followed by a short walk to the museum entrance. The Logan remains simpler because it is fully walkable.
And check the cancellation terms carefully. Give me the exact local deadlines and what happens after each one.

The Logan rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on Friday, October 16, 2026. After that, the penalty is one night including associated tax and the nightly fee. The Sofitel rate can be canceled without penalty until 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, October 15, 2026. After its deadline, the penalty is one night plus tax. Neither rate requires prepayment, though each property may place an incidental hold at check-in.
The Logan gives me one more day to cancel, but I don't think that is worth an extra $254.10 when the other route is direct.

That is the tradeoff. The Logan saves a short transit ride and has the later cancellation cutoff. Sofitel has the slightly higher Google rating, no mandatory property fee, and the lower all-in total, while still providing a direct Monday route.
Reserve the Sofitel, please. One room, one adult, checking in October 18 and checking out October 22. Use the traveler and payment details already on file.

Before I submit it: the refundable Sofitel reservation will be four nights at a complete quoted total of $1,057.98. Free cancellation ends at 11:59 p.m. Eastern on October 15, and a cancellation after that incurs one night's room charge plus tax. Shall I book it on those terms?

Booked. Sofitel Philadelphia at Rittenhouse Square is confirmed for Avery Thompson, one adult in one room, checking in Sunday, October 18, 2026 and checking out Thursday, October 22, 2026. The confirmed total is $1,057.98, with no mandatory property fee and no prepayment. Free cancellation is available through 11:59 p.m. Eastern on October 15; after that, the penalty is one night's room charge plus tax. Confirmation: SFP-824619. Your Philadelphia trip is now complete: both flights and all four hotel nights are confirmed.
